title: Scalar reduction for halfspace sensitivity
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=1$, and let $t,\theta\in\mathbb R$. The rotation sensitivity of the halfspace $\{z\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i\le t\}$ at angle $\theta$ equals the probability that independent standard Gaussian scalars $U,V$ disagree on whether they are at most $t$ after the rotation: $\Pr\bigl(\neg(U\le t\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\cos\theta\,U+\sin\theta\,V\le t)\bigr)$.
replaced: For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and independent standard Gaussian vectors $X,Y$, put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$. If $a\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $H=\{z:\sum_i a_i z_i\le t\}$, then $R_H(\theta)=\Pr(1_{(-\infty,t]}(U)\ne1_{(-\infty,t]}(\cos\theta\,U+\sin\theta\,V))$ for every real $t,\theta$, where $U,V$ are independent standard Gaussian scalars.
